_provenance: One month of market-wide stocks news as Moneycontrol published it. Headlines, standfirsts and section names are theirs, reproduced unchanged; the article stays on their site. A story is filed under this month by the publisher's own date where they gave one, and otherwise by the date this dashboard first saw it — so a story with `publishedAt: null` may sit one month later than it was published. Its own time is never invented: it stays null and renders as "time not published".

articles.title: Brent at $95 | Global bond yields cool off | Trump says not forcing Iran into talks | Opening Bell
articles.summary: US markets snapped a three-day losing streak, with the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq ending higher. Bond yields cooled slightly after touching fresh highs earlier in the session, while weaker-than-expected ADP payroll data shifted focus to Friday’s August non-farm payrolls report for clues on the US rate outlook. New York Fed President John Williams said rising yields reflect a strong US economy. The dollar index remained range-bound near 99.50, while oil prices stayed elevated, with Brent crude around $95 a barrel. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump said he was not trying to force Iran to the negotiating table and claimed the US has almost total control of the Strait of Hormuz. Asian markets are trading mixed, while GIFT Nifty points to a recovery at the Indian market open.

articles.title: Live: Choppy day for markets, oil above $92; Rupee recovers to 94.8/$ | Closing Bell
articles.summary: Indian equity markets remained under pressure, with the Sensex falling 200 points and the Nifty slipping below the 24,000 mark. Market breadth weakened further as declines outpaced advances, while most sectoral indices traded lower. FMCG and IT stocks emerged as relative outperformers in an otherwise choppy session. Auto stocks declined following the release of August monthly sales data, adding to the broader market pressure. The Nifty Midcap index snapped its two-day winning streak, while the Nifty Smallcap index extended its losses for another session. In commodities, Brent crude climbed back above $92 per barrel, keeping investors cautious amid ongoing global uncertainties. The rupee, however, recovered 28 paise to trade at 94.8 against the US dollar. Among Nifty 50 stocks, ITC, HCL Technologies and Adani Ports were the top gainers, while Shriram Finance, Maruti Suzuki and InterGlobe Aviation featured among the biggest losers.
